---
title: "METIS"
subtitle: "Configurable neural network surrogates for stochastic timeseries simulators"
toc: false
---

METIS is a Python package for training neural network surrogate (emulator)
models that stand in for expensive stochastic simulators. Instead of running
a slow simulator every time you need a sample, you train a model once and then
generate realisations cheaply.

Install METIS in your own project to load simulations, split your data, train
and evaluate a surrogate, and save it for later predictions. Use Python functions
in a notebook or script, or [Hydra](https://hydra.cc) configuration to swap
models, datasets and training settings by editing YAML. Both use the same package.

### Overview of METIS features

* Implementations of MLPs, Autoregressive Transformers, Flow Matching and Normalising Flows.
* Support for static parameter conditioning and sequence conditioning.
* Data loading from Parquet, data frames and arrays, with grouped train/validation/test splits.
* Evaluation and visualisation of predictions in the simulator's original units.
* Saved models that can be loaded in another script or application.
* Weights & Biases integration for hyperparameter sweeping and experiment tracking.

## How these docs are organised

We use the **SIRDS epidemic model throughout**, so you only need to understand
one simulator as you work through the examples.

- **[Basics of surrogate modelling](basics/motivation.qmd)** — what surrogate
  modelling is, the SIRDS example simulator, preparing data, installing METIS,
  a Hydra crash course, and training and saving your first models.
- **[Different kinds of surrogates](models/overview.qmd)** — the model families
  on offer, when to reach for each, and how their configurations work.
- **[Utilities and advanced features](utils/distributed-training.qmd)** — training on multiple GPUs.
- **[Sweeping](sweeping/overview.qmd)** — tuning hyperparameters with Weights & Biases.
- **[SBI](sbi/overview.qmd)** — using a trained surrogate for simulation-based inference.
- **[Reference](package/api.qmd)** — API details, troubleshooting and migration from older METIS work.
